title: BYD Overtakes Tesla as World's Top Grid Battery Storage Deployer in 2025
detail: Research firm Benchmark Mineral Intelligence reported on May 13, 2026 that BYD shipped over 60 GWh of battery energy storage systems (BESS) globally in 2025 — overtaking Tesla (46.7 GWh) as the world's leading grid storage integrator. BYD's 14.5 MWh HaoHan system, nearly three times the energy capacity of a single Tesla Megapack, combined with BYD's deep vertical integration across cells, packs, and power conversion systems, drove the shift. BYD has aggressively priced its grid storage systems in international markets, winning contracts in the UK, Germany, Australia, the Middle East, and across Asia-Pacific. Tesla, while still the leading grid storage company by brand recognition in Western markets, has faced margin pressure from Chinese competition and supply chain adjustments following its global gigafactory expansion. The overtake marks a structural shift in the global grid storage market: while Tesla pioneered utility-scale battery storage with the Hornsdale Power Reserve in 2017, Chinese manufacturers now command the largest deployment volumes. BYD's grid storage growth partially offsets softening passenger EV sales, making BESS a strategically important revenue stream for the company.

title: CIBF 2026 Opens in Shenzhen — World's Largest Battery Fair (3,200+ Exhibitors)
detail: The 18th China International Battery Fair (CIBF 2026) opened at the Shenzhen World Exhibition & Convention Center on May 13, 2026, running through May 15. The event — the world's largest battery industry exhibition — spans 280,000 square meters with more than 3,200 exhibitors and an expected 350,000 attendees. CATL, BYD, EVE Energy, Sunwoda, CBAK Energy, and BAK Battery all displayed new products at the event, spanning solid-state, sodium-ion, LFP, NMC, and vanadium flow chemistries. Key themes at CIBF 2026 included: (1) second-life battery systems (repurposing retired EV battery packs into grid storage), (2) AI-driven battery management systems, (3) next-generation solid-state and semi-solid-state cells with 400+ Wh/kg targets, and (4) ultra-fast-charging infrastructure enabling sub-10-minute charge times. The event serves as the de facto annual barometer of the global battery industry's state of technology, investment confidence, and competitive landscape, with product announcements from CIBF often setting the agenda for the following 12–18 months.

title: Moment Energy to Build World's Largest Second-Life EV Battery Factory in Vancouver in 6 Weeks
detail: Moment Energy announced on May 13, 2026 that it will construct the world's largest second-life EV battery repurposing megafactory in Vancouver, British Columbia — targeting completion in just six weeks. The Vancouver facility complements the company's 200,000 square foot primary gigafactory currently under construction near Austin, Texas. Moment Energy raised $40 million in a Series B funding round (closed May 5) led by Evok Innovations, with Liberty Mutual Investments, W23 Global, and Tokyo Gas's Acario division participating. Second-life battery repurposing involves disassembling retired EV battery packs and reconditioning or repackaging cells for use in stationary grid storage applications — data centers, hospitals, and commercial buildings — at substantially lower cost than manufacturing new cells. The BC facility will process retired battery packs from Canadian EV fleets (buses, commercial vehicles) that are reaching end-of-first-life after 8–12 years of operation. Moment Energy's model addresses two simultaneous challenges: the growing volume of EV batteries reaching end-of-first-life and the acute demand for affordable grid storage capacity from AI data centers and critical infrastructure operators.
